evals.prompt: Write Seedance dialogue direction for a Brazilian Portuguese confrontation between a CEO and a temp worker.
evals.expected_output: States Portuguese is natively supported and returns the dialogue in braces with delivery direction.
expectations: Reports a language-support verdict citing the native list.
Keeps approved dialogue inside curly braces and notes outside them.
Names register and variety for each speaker.
Does not add a pronunciation dictionary or request separate audio.

evals.prompt: The dialogue is in Hindi. How should I direct it for Seedance?
evals.expected_output: Flags Hindi as outside the native list and offers routes without claiming guaranteed pronunciation.
expectations: Identifies Hindi as not in the native list.
Lists annotation, a supported spoken language with subtitles, and audio-first as options.
Treats audio-first as requiring explicit user scope.
Does not promise correct pronunciation.

evals.prompt: In take 2 the actor says the wrong name in an otherwise perfect clip. Fix it.
evals.expected_output: Chooses a word-scoped repair and keeps the performance.
expectations: Verifies with a transcript diff and listening.
Proposes a retake with one cue or a word-only splice.
Refuses to re-voice the whole clip.
Bases splice acceptance on the actual speaker, local pitch and timing continuity, and listening rather than a universal percentage threshold.

evals.prompt: Rewrite my locked line so the model pronounces it more easily.
evals.expected_output: Does not change locked words without authorization.
expectations: Preserves the locked line as the selected text.
Shows any proposed alternative separately as a draft.
Offers delivery or annotation changes first.

evals.prompt: Two word-only repair candidates differ from their source by 8% and 12% in measured pitch. A listener hears a voice change in the 8% candidate but reports a natural match in the 12% candidate. Can the percentages alone decide approval?
evals.expected_output: Rejects a universal numeric gate and uses the actual voice, scope and listening evidence for a reviewed decision.
expectations: Does not automatically pass 8% or fail 12%, or cite a first production or four-splice anecdote as authority.
Flags the heard voice change and evaluates local pitch, timbre, timing and soundtrack continuity.
Requires scoped verification and mode-authorized approval rather than approving either candidate from the numbers alone.

evals.prompt: The splice is under 10% in pitch and tempo but no one can listen to it yet. Mark it passed.
evals.expected_output: Keeps listening and repair quality unresolved even though the numeric warning level is not exceeded.
expectations: Does not mark the repair passed from percentage measurements.
Records unavailable listening evidence as unresolved.
Preserves the source and correct speech pending review.
